# Core Features vs Nice to Have

#### Course: Rapid Build With Claude Code

## Core Features vs Nice to Have

This is where most projects get bloated. Every feature sounds important when you are excited about an idea. The discipline is in separating what the product cannot function without from what would be nice to add later.

For SpeedBlip, the must-have features were:

- Automatic background speed tests
- Download speed, upload speed, and ping measurement
- History log with timestamps
- Threshold alerts via browser push notification

The nice-to-have features that did not make the first build:

- ISP comparison data
- Multiple device tracking
- Export to PDF
- Team dashboards

Shipping SpeedBlip with only the must-haves was the right call. It is live, it works, and it solves the core problem completely. The nice-to-haves are a roadmap, not a blocker.

It is good practice to write your feature list in two columns - must-have and nice-to-have - before starting any design work. This single exercise prevents scope creep better than any process I know.
